To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 5-HT1A receptor agonist 8-OH-DPAT and 5-HT2 receptor antagonists LY53857 and ketanserin attenuate response suppression induced by the 5-HT precursor 5-HTP and the 5-HT receptor agonist DOI.

5-HTP, DOI, and LY53857 all produce operant response suppression when administered systemically and that 5-HT2 receptor antagonists block DOI-induced operant response inhibition when administered systemically, whereas LY53857 blocks operant response suppression produced by 5-HTP when administered centrally.
central administration of selective 5-HT2 antagonists attenuate operant behavior suppression induced with systemcally administered 5-HT2 receptor agonists or 5-hydrotryptophan.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the serotonin (5-hydroxy-tryptamine, 5-HT) system on operant responding in the rat.
the effects of the serotonin (5-HT) agonist, 5-HTP on operant behavior and the extent of central and peripheral mediation of these effects.
the effects of serotonergic agents on operant response suppression and the extent of central and peripheral mediation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the central 5-HT2C receptor is the major mediator of 5-HT-induced response suppression in this operant model.
5-HT2 receptor antagonists are effective in attenuating operant response suppression, but the exact mechanism of action remains unclear.
central 5-HT2 receptor antagonism blocks 5-HTP- and DOI-induced operant response depression in rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5-HTP model of operant response suppression appears to be mediated through central 5-HT2 receptors.
central 5-HT2 receptor antagonists block the effects of 5-HT agonists on operant behavior.
5-HTP and DOI-induced operant response inhibition is centrally mediated via 5-HT2 receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
central 5-HT2C receptors mediate DOI- and 5-HTP- induced response suppression, whereas the 5-HT1B/1D receptors mediate the effects of 5-HT1A receptors on operant response suppression.
central administration of selective serotoergic agents potently attenuate 5-HTP and DOI-induced operant response suppresion, suggesting a central mediation of these effects.
5-HTP can be used as a tool to study the effects of serotonergic drugs on behavior.
